If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to offset pessimism.  
If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon (day 8–15), reduce forecast by 2–4% for mid-horizon to reflect sentiment reversal.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast by 1–2% for late horizon (16–30) to prevent overcorrection.  
If sentiment is neutral and forecast is trending downward, increase forecast by 1–2% for late horizon (16–30) to prevent premature correction.  
If sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.33) in last 5 days, apply 0.5–1.0% smoothing adjustment across all horizons to dampen erratic forecast drift.
